𝐒𝐀𝐌𝐔𝐄𝐋 𝐋. 𝐉𝐀𝐂𝐊𝐒𝐎𝐍 𝐒𝐀𝐘𝐒 𝐏𝐔𝐋𝐏 𝐅𝐈𝐂𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍 𝐌𝐀𝐃𝐄 𝐇𝐈𝐌 “𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐂𝐎𝐎𝐋𝐄𝐒𝐓 𝐌𝐅 𝐎𝐍 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐄𝐓”⁣
 ⁣
“The first time I met Quentin was when I auditioned for Reservoir Dogs,” Sam said. “He and Lawrence Bender were reading with me and I was like, ‘Who the hell are these guys?’ I left thinking, yeah, I’m not getting this job.”⁣ ⁣ ⁣
⁣
Months later, at Sundance, he saw Reservoir Dogs for the first time and absolutely loved it. “I thought, maybe I made the biggest mistake of my life not getting that job.” But after that screening, Tarantino came up to him and said, “Hey man, you were great in that audition.” Jackson grinned: “Yeah, I was… So why didn’t I get the job?” They laughed, and Quentin promised, “I’m gonna write something for you.”⁣⁣
⁣
Not long after, Tarantino kept his word and sent him the script. Looking back on reading it for the first time, Jackson remembered thinking: “DAMN! This movie is amazing. I immediately flipped it back over and read it again to be sure I wasn’t making myself crazy, and I wanted to be in this movie so bad that I was making up that it was that good.”⁣
⁣
But even then, the role wasn’t completely his. Jackson later discovered that actor Paul Calderon had impressed Tarantino enough that he was suddenly in danger of losing Jules. Furious, Jackson flew to Los Angeles for another audition. He spent the flight studying the script, working out the relationships between the characters and preparing to prove the part belonged to him. This time, he left no doubt.⁣
⁣
Jackson got the role, and 𝐏𝐮𝐥𝐩 𝐅𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 changed everything. Jules Winnfield became one of the defining characters of his career, earned Jackson an Academy Award nomination and turned him into a star. Years later, Jackson admitted that it still surprises him that people consider him cool. “I was a square for so long and it totally amazes me that people think I am cool and Pulp Fiction had a lot to do what that.”⁣

source_details.title: Pulp Fiction
source_details.synopsis: Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary. It tells four intertwining tales of crime and violence in Los Angeles. The film stars John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis, Tim Roth, Ving Rhames, and Uma Thurman. The title refers to the pulp magazines and hardboiled crime novels popular during the mid-twentieth century, known for their graphic violence and punchy dialogue. Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction in 1992 and 1993, incorporating scenes that Avary originally wrote for True Romance (1993). Its plot occurs out of chronological order.
